script.text: Oil is back above 110 dollars. Why are stock futures falling with it?

Brent crude settled at 108.82 dollars on Wednesday, CNBC reports. Early Thursday it traded above 110. The National reports a Houthi drone attack near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry says operations were not affected.

The National also reports that Washington ordered non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia. Analysts quoted there link the oil price to the Iran war and risks around the Strait of Hormuz. Shaybah's pipeline carries crude to the Red Sea, bypassing that strait.

Stocks felt it. At 5:16 a.m. Eastern, Investing.com reported Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.8 percent, and S and P 500 futures down 1.0 percent. Tesla and Meta earnings also weighed, CNBC says. Futures can reverse before the open.
Will oil stay above 110 dollars next week? Yes or no?
